title: Reorder List
keyIdea: Three known pieces: find the middle (fast/slow), reverse the second half, then weave the two halves one node at a time. Only next pointers change; O(1) space.

approaches.name: Array of nodes + two indices
approaches.idea: Store all nodes in a vector; link nodes[i] → nodes[j] → nodes[i+1] … moving i, j inward; the meeting node gets next = NULL.
approaches.why: One pass to collect, one to relink, but the vector holds every node.

approaches.name: Middle + reverse + merge
approaches.idea: mid = middleNode(head); hs = reverseList(mid); weave hf and hs with temp; finally hf->next = NULL if hf remains.
approaches.why: Each step is a single pass over (part of) the list with a few pointers.

options: The order needs the last node, then the second-to-last…; reversed, they come from the front one by one

quiz.q: Why is temp saved before each relink?
options: Changing hf->next (or hs->next) cuts that node off from the rest of its half

quiz.q: What does the final "if(hf != NULL) hf->next = NULL" do?
options: Makes the last node of the new order point to NULL, so the list ends

quiz.q: Space of the array version vs this one?

steps: Can you return a new list, or must you relink in place? What about 1 or 2 nodes?
